recipes.name: Sanji’s Tuna Saute Inspired by One Piece
ingredients: For the Sweet Soy Caramelized Onions
Red food coloring (optional, as per user comment)
garnish: White sesame seeds + finishing salt
instructions: For the Sweet Soy Caramelized Onions

Heat oil in a medium skillet over medium heat. Add chopped onions and cook until they begin to brown. Add water to deglaze the pan, scraping up any browned bits. - 1 tbsp neutral oil (for sautéing) - 1 yellow onion finely chopped - water (as needed)

Continue cooking onions, adding water as needed, until they are golden brown (about 35-45 minutes). Add soy sauce, honey, and mirin, and stir to combine. Cook for 1-2 minutes until the mixture reduces and becomes jammy. Keep warm until ready to serve. - water (as needed) - 1 tbsp + 1 tsp soy sauce - 2 tsp honey - 2 tsp mirin
For the Seared Asparagus
Blanch the asparagus in a large pot of boiling water for 2 minutes, then transfer to an ice bath to cool for 1-2 minutes. Pat dry with paper towels. - 4 asparagus stalks trimmed

Heat vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add smashed garlic and asparagus, and cook for 1-2 minutes, or until the asparagus just starts to brown. Season with salt and pepper to taste. - 2 tbsp vegetable oil - 1 garlic clove smashed - 4 asparagus stalks trimmed - kosher salt (to taste) - freshly ground black pepper (to taste)
For the Paprika Tuile

In a medium bowl, combine water and neutral oil. Sift the flour, almond meal, and both sweet and hot paprika into the liquid mixture. Whisk to thoroughly combine. - 5 oz water - 3 oz neutral oil - 2 tbsp all purpose flour - 2 tbsp almond meal - 1 tbsp sweet paprika - 1 tbsp hot paprika
Heat a small nonstick pan over medium-low heat. Add 1-2 tablespoons of batter to the pan and cook until the tuile becomes crisp. Set aside to cool. - For the Paprika Tuile
If you wish to add vibrant color, mix red food coloring into the batter for a brighter appearance. - Red food coloring (optional as per user comment) - For the Paprika Tuile
For the Herb Oil

Blanch basil, parsley, and chives in boiling water for 15 seconds, then transfer to an ice bath to cool. Strain and dry the herbs. - ⅓ cup basil leaves packed - ⅓ cup parsley leaves + stems packed - ⅓ cup chive stems packed

Place the herbs in a food processor or mortar, add olive oil and a pinch of kosher salt. Process or muddle until partially pureed. - ⅓ cup basil leaves packed - ⅓ cup parsley leaves + stems packed - ⅓ cup chive stems packed - ½ cup extra virgin olive oil - pinch of salt
Pour the oil through a coffee filter into a glass vessel. Let the oil sit for 1 hour to fully strain. - For the Herb Oil
Refrigerate the oil until needed. Allow it to come to room temperature before using.
For the Tuna Sauté

Marinade: Place the tuna in a resealable bag, pour the marinade over it, and refrigerate for 30 minutes to 1 hour. - 7 oz slab bluefin tuna loin - ¼ cup soy sauce - 3 tbsp sake - 3 tbsp mirin - 1 ½ tbsp honey

Heat neutral oil in a large carbon steel skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering. Add the tuna and sear for 20-30 seconds on each side. Let the tuna cool on a plate for 5 minutes before slicing. - 2 tbsp neutral oil (for searing) - 7 oz slab bluefin tuna loin
For the Assembly

Serve the sliced tuna with Sweet Soy Caramelized Onion, Seared Asparagus, Paprika Tuile, and Herb Oil. Garnish with white sesame seeds and finishing salt. - For the Tuna Sauté - Sweet Soy Caramelized Onions (recipe above) - Seared Asparagus (recipe above) - Paprika Tuile (recipe above) - Herb Oil (recipe above) - garnish: White sesame seeds + finishing salt
